name: Italian Game: Giuoco Piano
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Bc5 4.c3 Nf6 5.d3 d6 6.O-O O-O 7.Re1 a6 8.Bb3
idea: Quiet and solid: c3 and d3 build the center, castle, Re1 supports e4, and Bb3 keeps the bishop safe from ...d5 or ...Na5.

name: Italian vs the Two Knights
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.d3 Be7 5.O-O O-O 6.Re1 d6 7.c3
idea: 4.d3 protects e4 and avoids sharp theory. Same plan: castle, Re1, c3, then think about d4.

name: White vs 3...Be7
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Be7 4.d4 exd4 5.Nxd4 Nf6 6.Nc3 O-O 7.O-O d6 8.h3
idea: The passive ...Be7 lets you open the center with 4.d4. Take back with the knight and develop freely.

name: White vs 3...h6
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 h6 4.d4 exd4 5.O-O d6 6.Nxd4 Nf6 7.Nc3 Be7 8.h3 O-O
idea: ...h6 wastes a move. Use the time: 4.d4 opens the center while Black's king is still in the middle.

name: White vs 3...Nd4 (trap)
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nd4 4.Nxd4 exd4 5.O-O d6 6.c3 dxc3 7.Nxc3 Nf6 8.d4
idea: 3...Nd4 sets a trap: 4.Nxe5?? Qg5! hits g2 and e5. Just take the knight with 4.Nxd4 and you're ahead in development.

name: Alapin vs 2...Nc6
pgn: 1.e4 c5 2.c3 Nc6 3.d4 cxd4 4.cxd4 d5 5.exd5 Qxd5 6.Nf3 Bg4 7.Be2 e6 8.Nc3 Qd7
idea: Take the full center with d4. If Black hits back with ...d5, recapture, develop with tempo on the queen, and keep a strong d4.

name: Alapin vs the Sicilian
pgn: 1.e4 c5 2.c3 Nf6 3.e5 Nd5 4.d4 cxd4 5.Nf3 Nc6 6.cxd4 d6 7.Bc4
idea: 2.c3 prepares d4 so you get a big pawn center. Kick the knight with e5, then develop fast.

name: Alapin vs 2...d6
pgn: 1.e4 c5 2.c3 d6 3.d4 Nf6 4.Bd3 Nc6 5.Nf3 Bg4 6.d5 Ne5 7.Nxe5 dxe5 8.Qb3 Qc7 9.Bb5+ Bd7
idea: Build the big center with d4 and Bd3. When ...Bg4 pins your knight, d5 kicks the c6 knight. If it goes to e5, take it: 7.Nxe5! and ...Bxd1 runs into Bb5+ and Nxd7. After 7...dxe5, Qb3 hits b7.

name: Alapin vs 2...d5
pgn: 1.e4 c5 2.c3 d5 3.exd5 Qxd5 4.d4 Nf6 5.Nf3 Bg4 6.Be2 e6 7.O-O Nc6 8.Be3
idea: Take on d5 and play d4. Black's queen is in the middle; develop calmly and castle.

name: Alapin vs 2...e6
pgn: 1.e4 c5 2.c3 e6 3.d4 d5 4.exd5 exd5 5.Nf3 Nc6 6.Bb5 Bd6 7.dxc5 Bxc5 8.O-O
idea: Against ...e6, go d4 and take on d5. Black ends up with an isolated pawn on d5 for you to target.

name: Advance French
idea: Lock the center with e5, support d4 with c3 and Nf3. a3 prepares b4 and keeps ...Qb6 and ...Bb4 tricks in check.

name: Advance French: 5...Bd7
pgn: 1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.e5 c5 4.c3 Nc6 5.Nf3 Bd7 6.Be2 Nge7 7.O-O Ng6 8.g3 Be7
idea: Keep the e5-d4 chain solid. Castle and use g3 to keep Black's knight out of f4.

name: Advance Caro-Kann
idea: Same space-grabbing idea as the French: e5, calm development, and Be3 to support d4.

name: Advance Caro-Kann: 3...c5
pgn: 1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.e5 c5 4.dxc5 e6 5.Be3 Nd7 6.Bb5 Qc7 7.Nf3 Bxc5 8.Bxc5 Qxc5 9.Nc3
idea: Take on c5 and hold it with Be3. Pin the d7 knight with Bb5 and develop quickly.

name: White vs the Scandinavian
pgn: 1.e4 d5 2.exd5 Qxd5 3.Nc3 Qa5 4.d4 Nf6 5.Nf3 c6 6.Bc4 Bf5 7.Bd2 e6
idea: Take on d5 and develop with tempo: Nc3 hits the queen. Then d4, Nf3, Bc4 and Bd2 with ideas of Nd5.

name: Scandinavian: 3...Qd6
pgn: 1.e4 d5 2.exd5 Qxd5 3.Nc3 Qd6 4.d4 Nf6 5.Nf3 a6 6.g3 Bg4 7.Bg2 Nc6 8.O-O O-O-O
idea: Develop with tempo, then fianchetto with g3 and Bg2 so your bishop hits b7 and the long diagonal.

name: Scandinavian: 2...Nf6
pgn: 1.e4 d5 2.exd5 Nf6 3.d4 Nxd5 4.Nf3 Bg4 5.Be2 e6 6.O-O Be7 7.c4 Nb6 8.Nc3 O-O
idea: Keep it simple: d4, Nf3, Be2, castle, then c4 to chase the knight away.

name: White vs 2...d6 (Philidor)
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 d6 3.d4 exd4 4.Nxd4 Nf6 5.Nc3 Be7 6.Bf4 O-O 7.Qd2 a6 8.O-O-O
idea: Against 2...d6, play 3.d4 and take the center. Develop everything, then castle long and push your kingside pawns.

name: White vs the Petrov
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nxe5 d6 4.Nf3 Nxe4 5.d4 d5 6.Bd3 Nc6 7.O-O Be7 8.c4 Nb4 9.Be2 O-O
idea: Take on e5, then retreat with 4.Nf3 before taking back on e4. Build with d4, Bd3, castle and c4.

name: White vs the Petrov: 3...Nxe4?
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nxe5 Nxe4 4.Qe2 Qe7 5.Qxe4 d6 6.d4 dxe5 7.dxe5
idea: If Black copies with 3...Nxe4?, 4.Qe2 hits the knight on the e-file. You come out a pawn up.

name: White vs ...d6 and ...g6 (Pirc)
pgn: 1.e4 d6 2.d4 Nf6 3.Nc3 g6 4.Be3 Bg7 5.Qd2 O-O 6.Bh6
idea: Big center, then Be3, Qd2 and Bh6 to trade off Black's best bishop. After that, h4-h5 against the castled king.

name: Modern: 1...g6
pgn: 1.e4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 d6 4.Be3 a6 5.Qd2 b5 6.f3 Nd7 7.h4
idea: Same plan as against the Pirc: big center, Be3 and Qd2, then f3 and h4 to attack.

name: White vs the Alekhine
pgn: 1.e4 Nf6 2.e5 Nd5 3.d4 d6 4.Nf3 Bg4 5.Be2 e6 6.O-O Be7 7.c4 Nb6
idea: Chase the knight with e5, then build the center with d4, Nf3 and c4. Simple space, no overextending.

name: White vs 2...f6 (Damiano)
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 f6 3.Nxe5 fxe5 4.Qh5+ Ke7 5.Qxe5+ Kf7 6.Bc4+ d5 7.Bxd5+ Kg6
idea: 2...f6 is a mistake: 3.Nxe5! and if 3...fxe5, Qh5+ starts an attack. Black's king gets hunted.

name: White vs 2...f5 (Latvian)
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 f5 3.Nxe5 Qf6 4.d4 d6 5.Nc4 fxe4 6.Nc3 Qg6 7.f3 exf3 8.Qxf3
idea: Take on e5, then retreat the knight to c4 when it's hit. Develop and open the f-file against Black's weakened king.

name: White vs 2...d5 (Elephant)
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 d5 3.exd5 e4 4.Qe2 Nf6 5.d3 Qxd5 6.Nbd2 Bf5 7.dxe4
idea: Take on d5. When ...e4 hits your knight, 4.Qe2 pins the pawn and wins it back with a better position.

name: White vs 1...Nc6
pgn: 1.e4 Nc6 2.d4 d5 3.e5 Bf5 4.Nf3 e6 5.Be2 Nge7 6.O-O h6 7.c3
idea: Take the center with d4, push e5 when Black plays ...d5, and develop like an Advance French.

name: White vs 1...b6 (Owen)
pgn: 1.e4 b6 2.d4 Bb7 3.Bd3 e6 4.Nf3 c5 5.c3 Nf6 6.Qe2 Be7 7.O-O
idea: Protect e4 with Bd3 and Qe2, take the center with d4 and c3, and castle.

name: White vs 1...a6
pgn: 1.e4 a6 2.d4 b5 3.Bd3 Bb7 4.Nf3 e6 5.O-O c5 6.c3 Nf6 7.Qe2
idea: Same idea as against the Owen: big center, Bd3 to guard e4, castle.

name: 4.d3: the quiet Italian
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.d3 Bc5 5.c3 d6 6.O-O O-O 7.h3 a6 8.Re1 Ba7
idea: The most common Italian at club level. Develop with ...Bc5 and ...d6, castle, then ...a6 and ...Ba7 so the bishop is safe from d4 and b4.

name: Two Knights: stop the Fried Liver
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.Ng5 d5 5.exd5 Na5 6.Bb5+ c6 7.dxc6 bxc6 8.Be2 h6 9.Nf3 e4 10.Ne5 Bd6
idea: When White's knight jumps to g5, hit back in the center with ...d5, then 5...Na5 chases the bishop instead of recapturing. You give a pawn for fast development.

name: Fried Liver: if you took on d5
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.Ng5 d5 5.exd5 Nxd5 6.Nxf7 Kxf7 7.Qf3+ Ke6 8.Nc3 Ncb4
idea: After 6.Nxf7, the king must walk to e6 to keep defending d5. 7...Kg8?? loses the queen, as in your game against ioanitux.

name: The fork trick
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.Nc3 Nxe4 5.Nxe4 d5 6.Bd3 dxe4 7.Bxe4 Bd6
idea: Against 4.Nc3, take on e4: if White takes back, ...d5 forks bishop and knight and you win the piece back with a strong center.

name: 4.d4: the open Italian
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.d4 exd4 5.e5 d5 6.Bb5 Ne4 7.Nxd4 Bd7 8.Bxc6 bxc6 9.O-O Bc5
idea: Take on d4, and when e5 hits your knight, strike back with ...d5. Your knight jumps to e4 and your bishops come out fast.

name: Ruy Lopez: the main road
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 a6 4.Ba4 Nf6 5.O-O Be7 6.Re1 b5 7.Bb3 d6 8.c3 O-O
idea: Against 3.Bb5, ask the bishop with ...a6, develop, then ...b5 and ...d6 keep e5 solid. Castle before anything sharp.

name: Ruy Lopez: quiet 5.d3
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 a6 4.Ba4 Nf6 5.d3 b5 6.Bb3 Be7 7.O-O O-O 8.c3 d6
idea: When White plays a slow d3, kick the bishop with ...b5, develop with ...Be7, castle and keep e5 solid with ...d6.

name: Ruy Lopez: 4.Bxc6 exchange
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 a6 4.Bxc6 dxc6 5.O-O f6 6.d4 exd4 7.Nxd4 c5 8.Nb3 Qxd1 9.Rxd1 Bg4 10.f3 Be6
idea: After the trade you have the two bishops. Guard e5 with ...f6, trade queens, and your bishops do the work in the endgame.

name: Scotch: main line
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 exd4 4.Nxd4 Nf6 5.Nxc6 bxc6 6.e5 Qe7 7.Qe2 Nd5 8.c4 Ba6 9.b3 g6
idea: Take on d4, hit e4 with ...Nf6. After e5, ...Qe7 pins the pawn, the knight goes to d5 and the bishop to a6 pressures c4.

name: Scotch: 4...Bc5
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 exd4 4.Nxd4 Bc5 5.Be3 Qf6 6.c3 Nge7 7.Bc4 O-O 8.O-O Bb6
idea: A simpler setup: ...Bc5 hits the knight, ...Qf6 adds pressure, then ...Nge7 and castle.

name: Scotch Gambit: 4.Bc4
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 exd4 4.Bc4 Nf6 5.e5 d5 6.Bb5 Ne4 7.Nxd4 Bd7 8.Bxc6 bxc6 9.O-O Bc5
idea: If White gambits with 4.Bc4, answer with ...Nf6. When e5 attacks the knight, hit back with ...d5 and go to e4.

name: Four Knights: 4.Bb5
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bb5 Bb4 5.O-O O-O 6.d3 d6 7.Bg5 Bxc3 8.bxc3 Qe7
idea: Copy White's setup: ...Bb4, castle, ...d6. When the bishop pins your knight with Bg5, trade on c3 and unpin with ...Qe7.

name: Four Knights: 4.d4
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.d4 exd4 5.Nxd4 Bb4 6.Nxc6 bxc6 7.Bd3 d5 8.exd5 cxd5 9.O-O O-O 10.Bg5 c6
idea: Take on d4 and pin the c3 knight with ...Bb4. After the trades, ...d5 gives you a strong center.

name: Four Knights: 4.Bc4 fork trick
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bc4 Nxe4 5.Nxe4 d5 6.Bd3 dxe4 7.Bxe4 Bd6
idea: Same fork trick from a different move order: ...Nxe4 then ...d5 wins back the piece with a fine center.

name: Vienna: meet f4 with ...d5
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.Nc3 Nf6 3.f4 d5 4.fxe5 Nxe4 5.Nf3 Be7 6.d4 O-O 7.Bd3 f5
idea: Against 2.Nc3 and 3.f4, strike with ...d5. Your knight on e4 is strong; back it up with ...f5.

name: Vienna: 3.Bc4
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.Nc3 Nf6 3.Bc4 Nc6 4.d3 Bb4 5.Nf3 d5 6.exd5 Nxd5 7.Bd2 Nxc3 8.bxc3 Be7 9.O-O O-O
idea: Against an early Bc4, develop with ...Nc6 and ...Bb4, then free yourself with ...d5. After the trades on c3, drop the bishop back to e7 and castle.

name: King's Gambit: 3...d5
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.f4 exf4 3.Nf3 d5 4.exd5 Nf6 5.Bc4 Nxd5 6.O-O Be7 7.d4 O-O
idea: Take the pawn, then hit back in the center with ...d5. Develop fast and castle; White's king is the one that's exposed.

name: King's Gambit: 3.Bc4
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.f4 exf4 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.Nc3 c6 5.Bb3 d5 6.exd5 cxd5 7.d4 Bd6
idea: Against the Bishop's Gambit, ...Nf6 hits e4, then ...c6 and ...d5 take the center.

name: Danish Gambit: decline with ...d5
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.d4 exd4 3.c3 d5 4.exd5 Qxd5 5.cxd4 Nc6 6.Nf3 Bg4 7.Be2 Bb4+ 8.Nc3 Bxf3 9.Bxf3 Qc4
idea: Against 3.c3, don't grab pawns. 3...d5 hits back in the center; after the queen recaptures, pin and pressure d4. This is the gambit that got you mated.

name: Center Game: 3.Qxd4
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.d4 exd4 3.Qxd4 Nc6 4.Qe3 Nf6 5.Nc3 Bb4 6.Bd2 O-O 7.O-O-O Re8
idea: When White takes back with the queen, ...Nc6 gains time on it. Develop fast, castle, then ...Re8 hits e4.

name: Bishop's Opening: 2.Bc4
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.Bc4 Nf6 3.d3 c6 4.Nf3 d5 5.Bb3 Bd6
idea: Hit e4 with ...Nf6, then build the center with ...c6 and ...d5.

name: Ponziani: 3.c3
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.c3 Nf6 4.d4 Nxe4 5.d5 Ne7 6.Nxe5 Nf6
idea: Hit e4 right away with ...Nf6 and take it. If d5 chases your c6 knight, go ...Ne7, and after Nxe5 bring the other knight back to f6. You keep the extra center pawn balance and develop with ...d6.

name: Early queen: 2.Qh5
pgn: 1.e4 e5 2.Qh5 Nc6 3.Bc4 g6 4.Qf3 Nf6 5.Ne2 Bg7 6.Nbc3 d6 7.d3 Bg4
idea: Defend e5 with ...Nc6 first, then block the f7 attack with ...g6 and ...Nf6. Every move you make gains time on the queen.

name: Queen's Gambit Declined
pgn: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5 Be7 5.e3 O-O 6.Nf3 h6 7.Bh4 b6
idea: Hold d5 with ...e6, develop, castle. ...h6 asks the bishop a question, and ...b6 prepares ...Bb7.

name: QGD: exchange 4.cxd5
pgn: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.cxd5 exd5 5.Bg5 c6 6.e3 Be7 7.Bd3 Nbd7 8.Qc2 O-O 9.Nf3 Re8
idea: After the exchange, build the Carlsbad setup: ...c6, ...Be7, ...Nbd7, castle and ...Re8. Solid and easy to play.

name: QGD: 5.Bf4
pgn: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Nf3 Be7 5.Bf4 O-O 6.e3 c5 7.dxc5 Bxc5 8.a3 Nc6
idea: Against Bf4, castle and strike with ...c5. Recapture with the bishop and develop the knight to c6.

name: Black vs the London
pgn: 1.d4 d5 2.Bf4 Nf6 3.e3 e6 4.Nf3 c5 5.c3 Nc6 6.Nbd2 Bd6
idea: Against the London, hit the center with ...c5 and challenge the f4 bishop with ...Bd6.

name: London: White keeps the bishop (7.Bg3)
pgn: 1.d4 d5 2.Bf4 Nf6 3.e3 e6 4.Nf3 c5 5.c3 Nc6 6.Nbd2 Bd6 7.Bg3 O-O 8.Bd3 b6 9.O-O Bb7 10.Qe2 Re8
idea: Castle, then ...b6 and ...Bb7, then ...Re8 to prepare ...e5 or ...Ne4. Watch White's bishop on d3 with the queen behind it: before ...g6 or ...h6, check for Bxh7+ or Bxg6 tricks (like 10.Bxg6 against you on Nov 23).

name: London: White trades (7.Bxd6)
pgn: 1.d4 d5 2.Bf4 Nf6 3.e3 e6 4.Nf3 c5 5.c3 Nc6 6.Nbd2 Bd6 7.Bxd6 Qxd6 8.Bd3 O-O 9.O-O e5
idea: If White trades bishops, you're comfortable. Take back with the queen, castle, then push ...e5: the queen on d6 supports it and your position opens up.

name: London: hit b2 with ...Qb6
pgn: 1.d4 d5 2.Bf4 Nf6 3.e3 c5 4.c3 Nc6 5.Nd2 Qb6 6.Qb3 c4 7.Qc2 Bf5 8.Qc1 e6 9.Ngf3 Be7
idea: Once the bishop leaves c1, b2 is weak: ...c5 and ...Qb6 attack it. After 6.Qb3, ...c4 gains space and ...Bf5 chases the queen. Use this ...c5 + ...Qb6 idea against any early Bf4.

name: Black vs 2.e3 (Colle)
pgn: 1.d4 d5 2.e3 Nf6 3.Nf3 e6 4.Bd3 c5 5.c3 Nc6 6.Nbd2 Bd6 7.O-O O-O
idea: Same plan as against the London: ...e6, ...c5, ...Nc6 and ...Bd6. c5 before Nc6 keeps your c-pawn free.

name: Torre: 3.Bg5
pgn: 1.d4 d5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Bg5 e6 4.e3 c5 5.c3 Nc6 6.Nbd2 Be7 7.Bd3 O-O
idea: Same plan as against the London and Colle: ...e6, ...c5, ...Nc6, ...Be7 and castle.

name: English: 1.c4
pgn: 1.c4 e5 2.Nc3 Nf6 3.Nf3 Nc6 4.g3 d5 5.cxd5 Nxd5 6.Bg2 Nb6 7.O-O Be7
idea: Answer 1.c4 with ...e5: it's a Sicilian with colors reversed. Take the center with ...d5 and retreat the knight to b6.

name: Black vs 1.Nf3 and g3
pgn: 1.Nf3 d5 2.g3 Nf6 3.Bg2 e6 4.O-O Be7 5.d3 O-O 6.Nbd2 c5
idea: Take the center with ...d5, ...e6 and ...c5, castle, and don't worry about White's quiet setup.

name: Black vs Nc3 + Bf4 (Jobava)
pgn: 1.d4 d5 2.Nc3 Nf6 3.Bf4 a6 4.e3 e6 5.Nf3 c5 6.Bd3 Nc6
idea: The Jobava's trick is Nb5 hitting c7. 3...a6 takes b5 away, then play your usual ...e6, ...c5 and ...Nc6.

name: Blackmar-Diemer Gambit: 2.e4
pgn: 1.d4 d5 2.e4 dxe4 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.f3 exf3 5.Nxf3 Bg4 6.h3 Bxf3 7.Qxf3 c6
idea: Take the pawn twice, then trade off the f3 knight with ...Bg4 and ...Bxf3. Calm ...c6 and ...e6 keep you a pawn up.

name: Levitsky: 2.Bg5
pgn: 1.d4 d5 2.Bg5 h6 3.Bh4 c6 4.e3 Qb6 5.b3 Bf5 6.Nd2 e6
idea: Ask the bishop with ...h6, then ...c6 and ...Qb6 hit b2 now that the bishop has left c1.

name: Bird: 1.f4
pgn: 1.f4 d5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.e3 g6 4.b3 Bg7 5.Bb2 O-O 6.Be2 c5 7.O-O Nc6
idea: Against 1.f4, take the center with ...d5 and fianchetto: your g7 bishop fights White's b2 bishop on the long diagonal.
